speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has the bleeding been spontaneous, or only after trauma like a fall or bump? Also, has he experienced any recent fevers, joint pain, or excessive fatigue?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Platelet Count, Peripheral Blood Smear.

speaker: Measurement
text:
RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC) - WBC: 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin: 12.1 g/dL, Platelets: 280,000 /μL (normal); Peripheral Blood Smear - No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells.

*Note: While the CBC and smear are normal, the clinical history of spontaneous bleeding and physical exam findings of petechiae, gum bleeding, and nasal crusting, combined with the special test finding of a deficiency in GIIb/IIIa receptors, indicate a functional platelet disorder (specifically Glanzmann's thrombasthenia) rather than a primary quantitative platelet deficiency.*
